bundle.text:
# dsh-ofm-balance bundle patch: inserts the plugin row into the web roster.
# One row mounts BOTH halves: the host side (gateway probe, cache, HTTP routes)
# and the browser side (the sidebar balance card).
- insert:
    - id: ofm-balance
      name: 'dsh-ofm-balance'

readme.text: **在 DSH 侧栏显示 [Our Free Model](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model)（OFM）网关各渠道的剩余额度。** > 一张常驻侧栏的小卡片，把「哪个渠道还有多少额度」摊开给你看。 [](README.md) [](README.en.md) [](package.json) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance) [](package.json) ---

折叠态 — 显示当前对话使用的渠道及其剩余百分比
展开态 — 每个渠道一行：进度条 · 剩余量 · 百分比

- **折叠态**：标题右侧显示**当前对话使用的渠道**及其剩余百分比，格式 `渠道名 · 百分比`。
  找不到当前渠道时就退回到剩余最少的那个渠道——那才是最该看的一个。
- **展开态**：每个渠道一行，含进度条、剩余量与百分比；数据来自网关的真实配额接口。
- **刷新**：点击「刷新」立即探测；页面可见时按周期自动轮询。

OFM 把十来个渠道（CodeArts、TRAE、Qoder……）挂在同一个网关后面。每个渠道各有自己的配额，
而网关默认只在你**主动去查**的时候才告诉你。于是很常见的两个问题：

- 「我刚才是走哪个渠道花的额度？」——折叠态直接回答。
- 「哪个渠道快用完了？」——按剩余量排序，一眼扫过去。

这张卡片把这两件事都放进侧栏，不占对话、不用点击、不打断你。

> **它同时支持两套 Our Free Model。** 「Our Free Model」这个名字下有两个产品：装在 DSH 里的
> [官方插件](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model)，以及独立的桌面应用。它们各自维护账号池，
> 互不相通。**默认读插件**——它跑在 DSH 里，账号就是在 DSH 里登录的那些；插件不在时自动回退读桌面应用。
> 详见 [数据来源](#数据来源)。

**默认只显示「已登录账号」的渠道**，其余按目录列出但隐藏，可在设置里手动打开。

判据是数据源自己的账号清单（`provider.status` → `accounts.total > 0`），不是 DSH profile 里
声明的模型 id。这一点在 0.7.0 改过，原因是旧判据在两个方向都会错：

- profile 是**快照**：账号早就没了，它还一直声明那个渠道，卡片于是堆满永远读不到数字的行；
- 刚登录的渠道**可能还没写进 profile**，真实账号反而被藏起来。

账号清单是实时真值，也是 `credits.balances` 唯一肯回答的前提。两个产品（插件 / 桌面应用）
的 `provider.status` 返回结构完全一致，因此一条规则覆盖两边。

| 来源 | 数据出处 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **已登录** | 数据源 `provider.status` → `accounts.total > 0` | 你在这个渠道登录了账号 |
| **目录** | 插件内置的渠道清单（与网关控制台一致，当前 13 个） | 该产品支持哪些渠道 |
| **已提供** | `GET /v1/models` → `data[].channel` | 此刻有模型可用 |
| **可读取** | `credits.balances` 返回了数字 | 此刻余额读得到 |

> **目录不是封闭的。** 如果数据源提供了目录里没有的渠道，它依然会被列出来并使用标题化的显示名。
> 上游新增渠道后，本插件无需更新即可工作——这一点有单元测试守着：
> `a freshly logged-in channel outside the catalogue still earns a row`。

| 情况 | 默认行为 |
| --- | --- |
| 已登录账号 | **显示**。即使此刻读不到余额，也保留该行并说明原因 |
| 目录中有、但没登录账号 | **隐藏**。可手动打开，用于盯一个以后可能会登录的渠道 |
| 已登录但读不到 | **显示**，并如实标注（如「网关未提供该渠道」） |
| 渠道未登录账号 | 查询成功但返回空账号列表，显示 **「未在该渠道登录账号」** |
| 无账号但手动打开 | **显示**，并提示「尚未登录该渠道的账号，仅供查看」 |

未登录账号的渠道会如实标注，而不是报错或留空——查得到和查不到是两件事，卡片把它们分开说。

在 DSH 的 **插件** 页打开本插件（`dsh-ofm-balance`）详情页，正文顶部的 **数据源** 与
**渠道显示** 区块即控制面板。渠道分成两组：

- **已登录账号** — 数据源里确实有账号的渠道
- **其余渠道（未登录账号）** — 目录中有、但还没有账号的

每个渠道一行，包含：

- 左侧复选框控制是否显示
- 渠道名与一行说明（已登录 / 未登录账号 / 当前未提供）
- 右侧状态标签

**勾选未登录的渠道时会弹窗确认**——那种渠道没有账号可读，现在不会有任何数字。
改动即时生效并写入 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-ofm-balance/settings.json`。

> **为什么不放在宿主自动生成的配置表单里**：DSH 会从插件的 `Config` schema 自动生成设置页，
> 但它只渲染标量字段；`array` 类型的渠道列表在那里渲染不出可用的复选框，也无法在
> 「显示未配置渠道」时给出确认对话。所以本插件自带面板。

readme.section: 为什么这个区块能排在「来源信息」之上
readme.text:
面板通过 `plugins.detail.section` 插槽注册，而该插槽是**追加**在官方页面自己的区块
（来源信息、当前版本、更新）之后的——注册时给的 `order` 只在槽位内部排序，改不了与官方区块的相对位置。

所以位置由两件事共同保证：

1. 详情页正文是 `flex-direction: column`，面板根节点设 `order: -1`，CSS 层面即可排到最前；
2. 渲染回调里再做一次保守的前插（仅当父容器确实是 flex column 时才动），作为 CSS 不可用时的兜底。

两者都不依赖宿主的内部排序实现。宿主若改变布局，面板会退回插槽给的位置，而不会报错。

也可以直接编辑 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-ofm-balance/settings.json`：

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "hidden": ["qoder"],
  "revealed": ["moonshot"]

| 字段 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `hidden` | 要隐藏的**已登录账号**渠道 |
| `revealed` | 要额外显示的**无账号**渠道 |
| `source` | 记住的数据源选择（`plugin` / `desktop`） |

删除该文件即恢复默认（已登录的全显示、无账号的全隐藏）。**被隐藏的渠道不参与探测，因此不浪费请求。**

进度条与百分比按**剩余比例**连续渐变——不是已用比例，也不是分档跳变。

色相经过实测调整。第一版把色相线性铺满整段，结果在健康区间显示一片看不出差别的绿色
（80% → 100% 只跨 23°）。现在改用锚点，把高位推向青色：

| 剩余 | 色相 | 观感 |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 100% | 178° | 青 |
| 90% | 147° | 春绿 |
| 80% | 123° | 绿 |
| 60% | 78° | 黄绿 |
| 40% | 48° | 琥珀 |
| 20% | 25° | 橙 |
| 0% | 0° | 红 |

饱和度与亮度也随数值变化，使整条刻度读起来是一条连续量表，而非色轮。
**语义不可翻转**：100% 永远是健康的青，0% 永远是红。

折叠态摘要里，渠道名保持默认文字色，**只有百分比着色**——两者都上色会让名字看起来像状态标签，与数字争夺注意力。

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance
```

也可以使用仓库地址或本地路径：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/绝对路径/dsh-ofm-balance
```

> 本机 profile 名不一定是 `web`，请替换成自己的（例如桌面端常见的是 `desktop`）。

readme.section: 预构建安装包（免构建授权）
readme.text:
每个版本都附带一个预构建的安装包，供插件市场直接提供：

```
https://github.com/Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance/releases/latest/download/dsh-ofm-balance.tgz
```

该文件名**不含版本号**，因此 `latest/download/` 在每次发版后仍然有效，不会像
「资产名带版本号」那样在下一个版本发布时静默 404。从该 tgz 安装时不需要源码构建，
因此也免去 `allowBuilds` 构建授权这一步。

手动安装：

1. 把本目录加入 profile 的 `package.json` → `dependencies`
2. 把包名 `dsh-ofm-balance` 追加到 `dsh.profile.bundles`
3. 在 profile 目录执行 `pnpm install`
4. 重启宿主

宿主半区改动需重启；客户端半区改动刷新页面即可。

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | 总开关；关闭后不探测、不注册路由 |
| `source` | `plugin` | 数据源：`plugin` 读 DSH 插件（默认主源），`desktop` 读桌面应用，`auto` 自动判定并在两套都在时询问 |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:18900` | 桌面应用的网关地址（`source=plugin` 时不用） |
| `credentialRoute` | `ourfreemodel` | 凭据与配置所属的 provider 路由名 |
| `pollIntervalSec` | `60` | 轮询间隔（30–3600 秒） |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | 单渠道超时。冷启动实测约 10.5 秒，不宜调低 |
| `hiddenChannels` | `[]` | （初始值）隐藏的已登录渠道 |
| `revealedChannels` | `[]` | （初始值）额外显示的无账号渠道 |

> 渠道开关的**实际值**存在 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-ofm-balance/settings.json`，由插件详情页的面板维护。
> 配置里的 `hiddenChannels` / `revealedChannels` 只作为首次运行的初始值。
> 数据源的**实际选择**也存在同一个文件里（`source` 键），优先级高于配置项——避免配置项与用户点击互相打架。

| 方法 | 路径 | 用途 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/overview` | 当前快照与探测报告 |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/refresh` | 立即探测并返回新快照 |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/channels` | 渠道分类结果（含显示名称），供设置面板使用 |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/visibility` | 保存渠道开关，请求体 `{ hidden, revealed }` |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/sources` | 数据源探测结果、当前选择、是否需要询问 |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/sources` | 切换数据源，请求体 `{ source: "plugin" \| "desktop" }` |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/view-session` | 报告侧栏正在显示哪个会话，请求体 `{ sessionId }`；用于让折叠态显示**该会话**的渠道 |

**有两套互不相通的 Our Free Model**，名字相同、账号各自独立，本插件会先探测再决定读哪一套：

| 数据源 | 是什么 | 怎么读 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin` | 安装在 DSH 里的 `dsh-our-free-model` 插件 | 内核 RPC 通道 `channel-pack`，方法 `credits.balances` |
| `desktop` | 独立的桌面应用（`127.0.0.1:18900`） | `POST {baseUrl}/api/management/channels/rpc` |

桌面应用还用它自己的接口发现渠道：`GET {baseUrl}/v1/models` → `data[].channel`；桌面路径的凭据取自宿主凭据服务的
`OURFREEMODEL_API_KEY`，**只在宿主进程内使用**。

readme.section: 为什么插件源必须走内核 RPC
readme.text:
官方插件有意把它的管理接口锁在 DSH 内核里：`/api/our-free-model/*` 与 `/api/channel-pack` 都要经过
`connection.admit()` 的浏览器令牌校验。实测从外部调用（包括回环地址、匹配的 Origin、以及从凭据库里取出
browser-session 密钥）**一律返回 401**。

但它把同一套接口注册成了进程内的 Fetch 路由，因此**同一个进程里的插件可以合法调用**——本插件的宿主半身
正是这样读取的：取 `connection` 服务、用共享的 owner Peer、向 `/api/channel-pack` 投递内核信封。

两套来源返回的积分结构**完全相同**，因此共用同一份归一化与分母修正逻辑，不存在两套算法漂移的问题。

**默认读插件**（`plugin`）——它跑在 DSH 里，账号就是在 DSH 里登录的那些，读它不需要另开进程。
因此正常情况下**不会问你**：

- 插件在 → 直接读插件，不打扰；
- 插件不在、桌面应用在 → 自动回退读桌面应用（不会显示空卡片）；
- 两套都在但你想自己选 → 把 `source` 设成 `auto`，首次运行时会问一次，之后记住；
- 在插件详情页可随时切换，选择写入 `settings.json`。

若已选的数据源后来不可用（应用关了、插件卸了），会自动回退到另一套，而不是把卡片钉在空结果上。

> **注意两套的账号池互不相通。** 卡片「正在使用的渠道」只认**当前所读那一套**的路由：
> 读插件时，走桌面网关的对话不会被点亮（反之亦然），因为那两套同名渠道背后是不同的账号，
> 点亮它会显示另一个账号的数字。

宿主启动时，插件会在凭据服务就绪之前挂载。本插件对此的处理：

- 探测拿不到凭据时**不缓存失败结果**，而是把渠道标记为「读取中」，1 秒后自动重试；
- 连续 3 次仍拿不到，才判定为真的未配置，并在卡片上给出可操作的提示（告诉你该配置哪个环境变量）；
- 网关的首次冷探测约需 10.5 秒，因此首次请求会立即返回带渠道名的占位行，数字随后填入——不会出现空白卡片。

结果：**打开 DSH 后无需手动刷新**，余额会自行出现。

- 网关**没有批量接口**，每次探测按渠道并发请求；隐藏的渠道不请求。
- `gemini` 的配额查询需要本机能访问 Google。未开代理时该渠道返回 `balance: null` 与
  `配额查询网络失败`，插件显示为「不可用」，**不影响其它渠道**；代理可用后下一轮自动恢复。
- 网关返回的积分包有两处会**算错百分比**，都以实测数据修正：

1. **重叠的 `used`**。同一个 `used` 会同时出现在聚合包与子包里（codearts 的「总积分包」与
     「赠送积分包」都是 349.31），把每个包的 `used` 相加会把分母从真实的 **7500** 抬到 7849.31。
     判别方式是找到 `remaining` 等于 `balance.total` 的那个包（即聚合包），用它**自己的** `used`。
  2. **失效的包**。网关把已过期的包标为 `active: false`（buddy 有 4 个失效裂变包，
     `total` 100 / `used` 100 / `remaining` 0）。它们已不属于本周期额度，计入分母会把
     4539 抬到 4939。

两者叠加后，codearts 从 91.1% 修正为 **95.3%**，buddy 从 78.9% 修正为 **85.8%**。
  当网关**完全没有**返回积分包明细、或返回值形状无法解释时，插件**不显示百分比**——
  没有可信的分母就不该编造一个数字（尤其是 100%，那会把「已用掉大半」显示成「从未使用」）。
- 未在某个渠道登录账号时，余额接口**仍可查询**，只是返回空账号列表；插件如实标注，不算失败。

| 决策 | 原因 |
| --- | --- |
| 宿主 / 浏览器半区分离 | API Key 只在宿主进程内使用，浏览器只见归一化后的快照 |
| `Promise.allSettled` 扇出 | 单个渠道慢或失败不能拖垮其它渠道 |
| 缓存优先 + 预热态 | 冷启动约 10.5 秒；首次请求立即返回占位行，避免首屏空白 |
| 凭据缺失时不缓存结果 | 冷启动时凭据服务晚于插件就绪，缓存「没有 key」会把一次瞬时状态变成永久错误 |
| 分类规则抽到 `lib/channels.js` | 纯函数、无 I/O，是策略所在，也最值得测试 |
| 渠道开关走 `plugins.detail.section` | 宿主自动表单渲染不了数组字段，也给不出「未配置渠道」的确认对话 |
| 开关存自己的 JSON 而非 profile 补丁 | 插件由 bundle 补丁挂载，profile 里没有它的行可改；写自己的文件不会破坏用户配置 |
| 显示名称由宿主下发 | 插件在提供未知渠道的网关部署上也能给出正确名称与标题化兜底 |

| 文件 | 职责 |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/gateway.js` | 网关协议：发现渠道、查询余额、归一化 |
| `lib/channels.js` | 渠道分类与可见性策略（纯函数） |
| `lib/service.js` | 缓存、轮询、凭据就绪重试、构建快照 |
| `lib/patch.js` | 渠道开关的持久化（原子写：先写临时文件再 rename） |
| `lib/index.js` | 宿主挂载、路由、配置、会话事件 |
| `lib/client.js` | 侧栏卡片 + 插件详情页的渠道开关面板 |

零运行时依赖。`@deepseek-ai/*` 全部由宿主提供，不作为 `dependencies` 声明。

插件内置的目录（与网关控制台一致）：

| id | 名称 | 所属 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codearts` | CodeArts | 华为云 |
| `buddy` | WorkBuddy 国内版 | 腾讯 |
| `workbuddy` | WorkBuddy 国际版 | 腾讯 |
| `lobsterai` | LobsterAI | 有道 |
| `qoder` | Qoder | 阿里系 |
| `qodercn` | Qoder 中国版 | 阿里系 |
| `trae` | TRAE | 字节 |
| `cline` | Cline | — |
| `loomy` | Loomy | — |
| `raccoon` | Raccoon | — |
| `minimax` | MiniMax Code | — |
| `zcode` | ZCode | — |
| `gemini` | Gemini | Google |

这份目录是**下限而非过滤条件**：未登录账号的渠道会如实显示，目录之外的渠道也会照常出现。

**Per-channel credit balances for the [Our Free Model](https://github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model) (OFM) gateway, shown in the DSH sidebar.** > One small always-on card that lays out "which channel still has how much left". [](README.md) [](README.en.md) [](package.json) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance) [](package.json) ---

Collapsed — the channel your current conversation is using, and what is left
Expanded — one row per channel: bar · remaining · percentage

- **Collapsed**: the channel your current conversation is using, with its remaining percentage, as
  `channel · pct`. When the current channel cannot be resolved it falls back to the channel with the
  least left — usually the one you actually want to look at.
- **Expanded**: one row per channel with a bar, the remaining amount and the percentage, read from
  the gateway's real quota endpoint.
- **Refresh**: click to probe immediately; when the page is visible the card polls on an interval.

OFM puts a dozen channels (CodeArts, TRAE, Qoder, …) behind a single gateway. Each one carries its own
quota, and the gateway only tells you when you go ask. Two questions follow:

- "Which channel did that request just spend?" — the collapsed card answers it.
- "Which channel is about to run out?" — sorted by remaining, one glance.

The card puts both in the sidebar: no conversation space, no click, no interruption.

The plugin lists **every channel the gateway supports**, not just the ones that currently have a
routable model.

This matters. `GET /v1/models` **only reports channels that have a model available right now**: a
channel with no logged-in account, or with no model currently servable, simply will not appear there —
yet it is still a supported channel, and its balance endpoint still answers. So the channel source
here is a full catalogue, with `/v1/models` used only as a supplement:

| Source | Where it comes from | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **configured** | the DSH profile's route entries: model ids declared under that route | you have models going through this channel |
| **catalogue** | the plugin's built-in list (matching the gateway console, 13 today) | which channels the gateway supports |
| **advertised** | `GET /v1/models` → `data[].channel` | a model is available right now |
| **readable** | the gateway's `credits.balances` returned numbers | a balance is readable right now |

> **The catalogue is a floor, not a filter.** A channel the gateway advertises but the catalogue has
> never heard of is still listed, under a title-cased display name. The plugin keeps working when the
> gateway adds a channel — and a unit test guards exactly that:
> `a channel outside the catalogue still appears when the gateway advertises it`.

| Situation | Default behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Configured channel | **Shown.** Even when the gateway cannot read a balance, the row stays and says why — you configured it, so hiding it would mislead |
| In the catalogue but not configured | **Hidden.** Can be turned on by hand to inspect those balances |
| Configured but unreadable | **Shown**, labelled honestly (e.g. "the gateway does not provide this channel") |
| Channel with no logged-in account | The query succeeds but returns an empty account list; shown as **"not signed in to this channel"** |
| Not configured but manually revealed | **Shown**, annotated "no models configured for this channel yet — inspection only" |

A channel with no account is labelled honestly rather than reported as an error or left blank:
"could not read" and "nothing there" are different facts, and the card keeps them apart.

Open the plugin's detail page on DSH's **Plugins** page; the **channel visibility** block at the top
of the body is the toggle panel. Channels are split into two groups:

- **Configured** — your DSH has models going through these
- **Other channels the gateway supports** — in the catalogue, not configured by you

Each row has:

- a checkbox on the left controlling visibility
- the channel name plus a one-line note (configured / no models configured in DSH / not currently offered by the gateway)
- a status chip on the right

**Revealing an unconfigured channel asks for confirmation**, because such a channel can only be
inspected, not used through this harness. Changes apply immediately and are written to
`$DSH_HOME/dsh-ofm-balance/settings.json`.

> **Why not the host's generated settings form?** DSH derives a settings page from the plugin's
> `Config` schema, but it renders scalar fields only; an `array` channel list gets no usable
> checkboxes there, and it cannot ask the confirmation question when revealing an unconfigured
> channel. So this plugin ships its own panel.

readme.section: Why the block can sit above "Source information"
readme.text:
The panel registers through the `plugins.detail.section` slot, which is **appended after** the
official page's own blocks (source information, current version, updates) — the `order` given at
registration sorts within the slot only and cannot change the position relative to official blocks.

So the position is guaranteed by two things together:

readme.section: Why the block can sit above "Source information"
readme.text:
1. the detail page body is `flex-direction: column`, and the panel's root carries `order: -1`, which
   sorts it first at the CSS level;
2. the render callback performs one conservative prepend (only when the parent really is a flex
   column), as a fallback for when CSS is unavailable.

Neither depends on the host's internal ordering. If the host changes its layout the panel falls back
to the position the slot gave it, rather than erroring.

You can also edit `$DSH_HOME/dsh-ofm-balance/settings.json` directly:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "hidden": ["qoder"],
  "revealed": ["moonshot"]

| Field | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `hidden` | **Configured** channels to hide |
| `revealed` | **Unconfigured** channels to additionally show |

Delete the file to restore defaults (all configured shown, all unconfigured hidden).
**Hidden channels are not probed, so they cost no requests.**

The bars and percentages follow the **remaining** ratio as a continuous gradient — not the consumed
ratio, and not a stepped scale.

The hue was tuned against real data. The first version spread the hue linearly across the whole
range, which produced an indistinguishable band of green through the healthy end (80% → 100% spanned
only 23°). It now uses anchors that push the top of the range toward cyan:

| Remaining | Hue | Reading |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 100% | 178° | cyan |
| 90% | 147° | spring green |
| 80% | 123° | green |
| 60% | 78° | yellow-green |
| 40° | 48° | amber |
| 20° | 25° | orange |
| 0% | 0° | red |

Saturation and lightness vary with the value too, so the scale reads as a continuous gauge rather
than a colour wheel. **The semantics never invert**: 100% is always healthy cyan, 0% always red.

In the collapsed summary, the channel name keeps the default text colour and **only the percentage is
tinted** — colouring both makes the name read like a status label and competes with the number.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance
```

A repository URL or a local path works just as well:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-ofm-balance
```

> Your profile may not be called `web`; substitute your own (desktop builds commonly use `desktop`).

Every release carries a prebuilt archive so storefronts can offer it directly:

```
https://github.com/Shen-18/dsh-ofm-balance/releases/latest/download/dsh-ofm-balance.tgz
```

The asset name carries **no version**, so `latest/download/` keeps working after every release
instead of silently 404ing the way a versioned filename does once you cut the next one. Installing
from that tgz needs no source build, which also skips the `allowBuilds` approval step.

Manual install:

1. add this directory to the profile's `package.json` → `dependencies`
2. append the package name `dsh-ofm-balance` to `dsh.profile.bundles`
3. run `pnpm install` in the profile directory
4. restart the host

Host-half changes need a restart; browser-half changes need only a page refresh.
Deployment-level settings on the host side (in the profile patch or the plugin's config):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; when off, nothing is probed and no route is registered |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:18900` | gateway address |
| `credentialRoute` | `ourfreemodel` | the provider route the credential and configuration belong to |
| `pollIntervalSec` | `60` | poll interval (30–3600 s) |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | per-channel timeout. Cold start measured around 10.5 s; do not lower it much |
| `hiddenChannels` | `[]` | (initial value) configured channels to hide |
| `revealedChannels` | `[]` | (initial value) unconfigured channels to additionally show |

> The **live** toggle values live in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-ofm-balance/settings.json`, maintained by the
> detail-page panel. `hiddenChannels` / `revealedChannels` in the config are first-run initial values.

Every route is **loopback-only** (anything other than `127.0.0.1` / `::1` gets a `403`). The API key
is resolved by the host and never sent to the browser.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/overview` | current snapshot and probe report |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/refresh` | probe now and return a fresh snapshot |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/channels` | the channel classification (with display labels) for the settings panel |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-ofm-balance/visibility` | persist the channel toggles, body `{ hidden, revealed }` |

The host side talks to the local gateway directly:

| Purpose | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| discover channels | `GET {baseUrl}/v1/models` → `data[].channel` |
| query a balance | `POST {baseUrl}/api/management/channels/rpc`, method `credits.balances`, params `{ provider }` |

The credential is read from the host credential service as `OURFREEMODEL_API_KEY` and **used only
inside the host process**.
The result: **balances appear on their own after DSH opens**, with no manual refresh.

- The gateway has **no batch endpoint**, so each probe fans out per channel; hidden channels are not
  requested at all.
- `gemini`'s quota query needs the machine to reach Google. Without a proxy that channel returns
  `balance: null` with a network-failure note, is shown as "unavailable", and **does not affect other
  channels**; it recovers on the next round once a proxy is available.
- Two properties of the gateway's credit bundles make the percentage go wrong, both corrected
  against measured data:

1. **Overlapping `used`**. The same `used` figure appears in both an aggregate bundle and its
     children (codearts' 总积分包 and 赠送积分包 both report 349.31), so summing every bundle's
     `used` inflates the divisor from the true **7500** to 7849.31. The fix identifies the bundle
     whose `remaining` equals `balance.total` — the aggregate — and uses **that bundle's own**
     `used`.
  2. **Lapsed bundles**. The gateway marks expired bundles `active: false` (buddy carries four
     lapsed 裂变包 at `total` 100 / `used` 100 / `remaining` 0). They are no longer part of the
     current cycle's allowance, and counting them inflates 4539 to 4939.

Together these move codearts from 91.1% to the correct **95.3%** and buddy from 78.9% to
  **85.8%**. When the gateway returns no bundle detail at all — or a shape the plugin cannot
  explain — the percentage is omitted rather than fabricated, because there is no denominator to
  trust and a made-up 100% would show a mostly-spent balance as never used.
- When no account is signed in for a channel, the balance endpoint **still answers** and simply
  returns an empty account list; the plugin labels it honestly rather than counting it as a failure.

| Decision | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Split host / browser halves | the API key stays inside the host process; the browser only sees a normalised snapshot |
| `Promise.allSettled` fan-out | one slow or failing channel must not drag the others down |
| Cache-first with a warm-up state | cold start is ~10.5 s; the first request returns placeholder rows to avoid a blank first paint |
| A missing credential is not cached | at cold start the credential service comes up after the plugin, so caching "no key" turns one transient state into a permanent error |
| Classification rules extracted to `lib/channels.js` | pure functions, no I/O: that is where the policy lives and what is most worth testing |
| Channel toggles go through `plugins.detail.section` | the host's generated form cannot render array fields, nor ask the "unconfigured channel" confirmation |
| Toggles stored in their own JSON rather than the profile patch | the plugin is mounted by a bundle patch, so there is no row in the profile to edit; writing its own file cannot damage the user's config |
| Display labels come from the host | the plugin still names channels correctly on gateway deployments that offer unknown ones, falling

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/gateway.js` | gateway protocol: channel discovery, balance queries, normalisation |
| `lib/channels.js` | channel classification and visibility policy (pure functions) |
| `lib/service.js` | cache, polling, credential-readiness retry, snapshot building |
| `lib/patch.js` | persistence of the channel toggles (atomic: temp file then rename) |
| `lib/index.js` | host mounting, routes, configuration, session events |
| `lib/client.js` | the sidebar card and the detail-page channel toggle panel |

```bash
npm run check   # syntax check (node --check)
npm test        # unit tests: channel classification + settings persistence (node --test)
```

The tests cover the classification policy and the boundary cases of settings persistence (missing
file, corrupt file, atomic write, tolerance of unknown shapes). They need no network and spend no
quota.

- **0.8.4** — fixed the **collapsed strip showing another session's channel**. The sidebar card is one
  element **shared by every conversation**, but the route memory was a single global value: the
  `session/event` callback is `(session, event)` and the session argument was ignored (named
  `_session`). With two sessions open, the card therefore named the channel of **whichever session had
  sent a request most recently**, not the one on screen — measured: the strip said `buddy` while the
  transcript was on `codearts`.
  Routes are now recorded per session from `session.id`, and the client reads the main-view session
  (`retainedBy.mainView`) from the shell's `sessions` service and reports it via `POST /view-session`,
  so the strip only names that session's channel. A viewed session that has not sent a request yet
  shows nothing rather than another session's channel. A shell without the `sessions` service falls
  back to the old global behaviour instead of going blank (`sessions` is deliberately not listed in
  `inject` — Cordis treats those as required dependencies, and a missing one would deactivate the
  plugin). 6 new tests (102 total).
